newsitem.title: UK: London freight - U.S. Gulf panamaxes face trouble.
newsitem.headline: London freight - U.S. Gulf panamaxes face trouble.

text.p: London, March 7 (reuter) - An 11 point rise in the Baltic Freight Index (BFI) to 1,430 disguised difficulties facing early panamaxes in the U.S. Gulf, brokers said.
Prompt tonnage was said to be prepared to wait up to 10 days for suitable business, but early stems were in short supply.
The BFI panamax routes based on estimated rates for loading 10-30 days ahead, have all edged forward.

The caper market was generally lacking impetus and direction, while the handy-sizes in contrast are enjoying a boom in demand from grain charterers in the Plate and Brazil, and firmer rates have been reported from U.S. Gulf.
The Continent and in the Far East are also experiencing firmer rates.
GRAIN - A few early panamaxes were said to be suffering from lack of demand for March positions in the U.S. Gulf and prompt rates have suffered accordingly.
Toepfer fixed Saturn V 62,212 dwt for heavy grain for mid March from U.S. Gulf to Portugal at $11.50 option Spain at $12.00 but failed on stem.
Forward positions are said to look more promising for owners with first half April U.S. Gulf/Japan generally reckoned to be worth no less than $24.25 no combo.

Brokers believed the Plate market was merely moving sideways after Cargill reported fixing the 1977-built Velos 2.6m cft grain Paranagua/Holland for March 15/20 at a lumpsum equivalent of $16.35 basis 53'.
Brokers reported charterers such as Pan Ocean, Halla and Daiichi quoting fresh Plate/Far East grain requirements for first half April.
The most significant grain activity now emerging concerns handies from Argentina and Brazil. Seaboard (Comshipco) fixed the 1973-built Christos M for 25,000/5 maize Plate/Casablanca spot at $24.00.
This business two to three weeks ago was being covered at about $18.00.

Few detailed fixtures have so far been reported in this area but brokers believe sharply increased rates have been agreed for handies from the Plate to S.Africa, for example and also to Malaysia (possibly at about $42.00).

MINERALS - Little fresh chartering news emerged in the caper market, but BHP was reported to be continuing their iron ore activities from Port Hedland to Constanza. Three vessels were said to have been covered so far with a fourth under negotiation.
Brokers believed BHP have already taken Tai Shan 149,516 dwt delivery China early April at $14,100 daily and both Hanjin Capetown and Leopold Ld for 150,000 tonnes at $8.85.
Some reports put the Leopold Ld rate at $9.25.

Pacific panamax rates continued firm for trips (especially to the Atlantic) and short period. British Steel were thought to have paid as much as $7,750 daily for Clymene 65,000 dwt for prompt delivery Far East via Roberts Bank to UK.
Aimcor WAS reported to have covered a panamax delivery Far East for a trip via US West Coast to the Continent with petroluem coke at $8,250 daily.

K Line took the 1983-built Red Cherry 66,980 dwt delivery Taiwan mid March for a trip via W.Australia to Japan at a firm $11,000 daily, and Deiulemar paid an improved $8,150 daily for Michele Iulia 64,850 dwt delivery prompt Muscat for S.African coal to Italy.
Navix booked Sea Diamond 69,220 dwt delivery Nagoya mid March for four to six months at a solid $11,850 daily.
Reports that Hai Kang 70,155 dwt was fixed delivery Philippines end March for three to five months at $11,750 daily were not substantiated.
HANDIES - Good quality tonnage was said to be in decreasing supply in the Far East, partly because delays in Australian grain loading ports has tied up so many vessels.
Brokers expect rates to rise in this area for modern types.
There was optimistic reports also from owners/brokers with geared tonnage on the Continent where plenty of fresh business was said to be available.

One over-age vessel of about 25,000 dwt was said to have been fixed to the Mideast Gulf at over $10,000 daily, and an over-age 22,300 dwt fortune type was thought to have gone for around two to four months redelivery Atlantic at close to $5,250 daily.
